#ukulele #teaching

Teaching my niece Eilidh (9) on her Kala KA-15S soprano, Saturdays at 11. Pattern one is D-D-U-U-D-U (the "island strum"), at 70 BPM, counting "1, 2-and, and-4-and" out loud because she skips the up on the and of 3. She keeps strumming with her thumb nail and it sounds like a cheese grater, so we switched to the side of the index finger, wrist loose, movement from the forearm. Songs so far: "Riptide" (C, Am, G, F, the F is fine on uke, not like guitar), "You Are My Sunshine" in 3/4 with D-D-U-D-U. Next week: chunking (the muted chop on 2 and 4). Strings are Aquila Nylgut, re-tuned every five minutes for the first week, settled after that. Fun to teach after [[Guitar practice]], the opposite of serious. Later on she might like [[Chord progressions]] explained with the four pop chords.
